next_question: Should the product lane pivot to measuring end-to-end amortized cost for C-PRODUCT-ECON (mechanism deduplication savings across tasks where fewer unique mechanisms to store/retrieve offset per-mechanism token penalty), or close token-based inheritance viability entirely and pursue alternative product economics (retrieval efficiency, registry size compression)?
why_next: Token savings are falsified for both short (parent -6.4%) and long (this experiment, bimodal 2/5 positive) value URL patterns under tiktoken cl100k_base. The per-mechanism token-cost argument for parameterized inheritance is closed. The only remaining economic path is orthogonal: amortized deduplication across tasks (C-PRODUCT-ECON) where fewer unique mechanisms reduce storage, retrieval and transmission costs independent of per-mechanism token count. This requires end-to-end measurement with real model calls, browser, retrieval and verification — a materially different experiment. Alternatively, if deduplication economics are also non-viable, C-PRODUCT-ECON should be closed and the product lane should pursue alternative mechanisms entirely.

established: Resolve/bind pipeline validated for manually-registered parameterized mechanisms with 1-3 slots on committed code: resolve() returns EXECUTABLE with correct bound_action when required_slots satisfied (5/5 long-value + 2 controls = 7/7), UNKNOWN when missing (7/7), _bind() substitutes correctly for 1-3 vars, kernel regression 3/3 intact (kernel.py sha256=30b741 or 084bf58 base)

Token savings DO exist for single-slot patterns with genuinely long per-slot concrete values under tiktoken cl100k_base: UUID 36-char saves 44.44% (36→20 tokens), bearer 64-char saves 56.72% (67→29 tokens). These are the only two patterns where per-slot concrete value exceeds template overhead (slot_name + 3 chars)

Token penalty confirmed for short-value (1-3 char numeric) URL patterns across two independent experiments: parent mean -6.4% (5 patterns), this experiment PC_SHORT -5.26% (1 pattern). Root cause: ${varname} syntax adds varname.length+3 chars overhead per slot, exceeding short concrete values

Token savings do NOT exist as a general claim for long-value patterns: 2/5 patterns positive, 2/5 negative, 1/5 neutral under frozen ALL-must-pass decision rule. The hypothesis that template overhead is universally dominated by long concrete values is falsified

Multi-slot patterns with short per-slot values incur net token penalty even at long total string length: P3_DEEPPATH 2-slot -11.54%, P5_MULTIPARAM 3-slot -9.68%. Slot count is the primary causal factor, not total string length
